title: And, bhikkhus, when that bhikkhu has dwelt in these five things, four more things should be developed. The perception of foulness should be developed to…
content: And, bhikkhus, when that bhikkhu has dwelt in these five things, four more things should be developed. The perception of foulness should be developed to abandon greed; loving-kindness should be developed to abandon hatred; mindfulness of breathing should be developed to cut off thoughts; the perception of impermanence should be developed to uproot conceit. Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu with the perception of impermanence, the perception of non-self becomes established; for a bhikkhu with the perception of non-self, conceit is uprooted, and in this very life he attains Nibbāna.

title: For one who has no 'I' and 'mine' in regard to name-and-form, Who does not grieve over what is not, That one is truly called…
content:
For one who has no 'I' and 'mine' in regard to name-and-form,
Who does not grieve over what is not,
That one is truly called a bhikkhu.

A bhikkhu who dwells in loving-kindness,
With faith in the Buddha's teaching,
Attains the peaceful state,
The blissful state of peace.

Bhikkhu, empty this boat;
Empty, it will go quickly.
Having cut off greed and hatred,
You will go to Nibbāna.

title: Māluṅkyaputta, there are these four births of craving from which craving arises for a bhikkhu. What four? Either because of robes, Māluṅkyaputta, craving arises, from…
content: Māluṅkyaputta, there are these four births of craving from which craving arises for a bhikkhu. What four? Either because of robes, Māluṅkyaputta, craving arises, from which craving arises for a bhikkhu. Or because of almsfood... or because of lodging... or because of this or that kind of existence. Māluṅkyaputta, there are these four births of craving from which craving arises for a bhikkhu. When, Māluṅkyaputta, craving is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made non-existent, unable to arise in the future — then, Māluṅkyaputta, that bhikkhu is called one who has destroyed craving, untied the fetters, rightly demolished conceit, and made an end of suffering.

title: Just as, bhikkhus, a lake that is clear, bright, not stirred up. A person with good eyes standing on the bank can see the oysters,…
content: Just as, bhikkhus, a lake that is clear, bright, not stirred up. A person with good eyes standing on the bank can see the oysters, the shells, the gravel, the pebbles, the schools of fish moving about and resting. Why is that? Because the water is not stirred up, bhikkhus. So too, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu with a mind not stirred up can know his own benefit, can know the benefit of others, can know the benefit of both, can realize a superior human state, the truly noble distinction of knowledge and vision — this is possible. Why is that? Because the mind is not stirred up, bhikkhus.

title: Cunda, that a person who is himself sunk in mud could pull out another sunk in mud — this is impossible. Cunda, that a person…
content: Cunda, that a person who is himself sunk in mud could pull out another sunk in mud — this is impossible. Cunda, that a person who is not sunk in mud could pull out another sunk in mud — this is possible. Cunda, that a person who is not tamed, not trained, not fully liberated, could tame, train, and fully liberate another — this is impossible. That a person who is tamed, trained, fully liberated, could tame, train, and fully liberate another — this is possible.

title: Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa, in the presence of the Blessed One, spoke these appropriate verses in praise: 'Today is the pure fifteenth, Five hundred bhikkhus…
content:
Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa, in the presence of the Blessed One, spoke these appropriate verses in praise:

'Today is the pure fifteenth,
Five hundred bhikkhus have gathered,
The noble ones have cut the fetters,
Without afflictions, ended rebirth.

Like a Wheel-turning Monarch,
With ministers attending him,
Travels all the four directions,
From this land to the ocean's edge.

So too, the disciples,
Who have attained the three knowledges,
Have slain death,
These ones attend upon
The victor in battle,
The supreme caravan leader.

All are sons of the Blessed One,
None is useless.
I reverently pay homage
To the one who has pulled out the dart of craving,
I respectfully honor
The one of the sun's lineage.'

title: Possessing these four qualities, bhikkhus, as such is placed in hell. What four? Possessing evil bodily action, evil verbal action, evil mental action, and being…
content:
Possessing these four qualities, bhikkhus, as such is placed in hell. What four? Possessing evil bodily action, evil verbal action, evil mental action, and being ungrateful, unthankful. Possessing these four qualities, bhikkhus, as such is placed in hell.
Possessing these four qualities, bhikkhus, as such is placed in heaven. What four? Possessing good bodily action, good verbal action, good mental action, and being grateful, thankful. Possessing these four qualities, bhikkhus, as such is placed in heaven.

title: One who is skilled in the goal, One who knows the peaceful path, Should act like this: After understanding clearly, Being capable, upright, Truly, well…
content:
One who is skilled in the goal,
One who knows the peaceful path,
Should act like this:
After understanding clearly,
Being capable, upright,
Truly, well direct, easy to speak to,
Gentle, without conceit.

Content, easily supported,
With few duties, living simply,
With peaceful faculties, wise,
Not arrogant, without greed for families.

One should not commit any trivial fault
That other wise people might criticize.
May all beings be happy and secure,
May they attain happiness and well-being.

Whatever living beings there are,
Frail or strong, without exception,
Long or large, medium or short,
Subtle or gross, seen or unseen,
Those living far or near,
Those already born or seeking birth,
May all beings be happy and well.

title: Māluṅkyaputta, just as a man shot with a dart thickly smeared with poison. His friends and relatives summon a surgeon. But the man says: 'I…
content: Māluṅkyaputta, just as a man shot with a dart thickly smeared with poison. His friends and relatives summon a surgeon. But the man says: 'I will not have this dart removed until I know whether the man who shot me was a noble, a brahmin, a merchant, or a worker.' He might say: 'I will not have this dart removed until I know the name and clan of the man who shot me.' He might say: 'I will not have this dart removed until I know whether the man who shot me was tall, short, or of medium height.' He might say: 'I will not have this dart removed until I know whether the man who shot me was dark, tawny, or golden.' ... Māluṅkyaputta, that man would die and still not know these things. So too, Māluṅkyaputta, whoever says: 'I will not live the holy life under the Blessed One until he answers me: "The world is eternal" or "the world is not eternal" ... "the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death" — that person will die and still not have had these things answered by the Tathāgata. Māluṅkyaputta, the holy life does not depend on the view that the world is eternal. The holy life does not depend on the view that the world is not eternal. Whether there is the view that the world is eternal or the view that the world is not eternal, there is still birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, and I teach their abandonment here and now.

title: Just as, bhikkhus, a tree with its branches and leaves destroyed: then its shoots do not reach completeness, its bark does not reach completeness, its…
content: Just as, bhikkhus, a tree with its branches and leaves destroyed: then its shoots do not reach completeness, its bark does not reach completeness, its sapwood does not reach completeness, its heartwood does not reach completeness. So too, bhikkhus, for an immoral person, one of broken virtue, right concentration is thereby destroyed. When right concentration is absent, for one whose right concentration is destroyed, true knowledge and vision of things as they really are is thereby destroyed. When true knowledge and vision is absent, for one whose true knowledge and vision is destroyed, disenchantment and dispassion are thereby destroyed. When disenchantment and dispassion are absent, for one whose disenchantment and dispassion are destroyed, the knowledge and vision of liberation is thereby destroyed.
